rows.note: Faint CME observed to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, not observed in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap. The source is likely far-sided over the east limb, potentially observed as field line movement in GOES SUVI 284 around 2026-10-25T23:06Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2 only plane-of-sky.

rows.note: This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. This CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2 in real time due to a data gap. The source may be related to an opening of field lines visible over the western limb in SDO AIA 171 imagery starting around 2026-10-25T23:55Z, likely associated with a small eruption from Active Region 14560 (N14W75).

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the source longitude.

rows.note: This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. There is a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery at the time of this CME. The source may be related to a small eruption from Active Region 14560 (N14W75) seen best in SDO AIA 131/193/304 imagery starting around 2026-10-26T01:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the source longitude.

rows.note: CME observed to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the SE in STEREO A COR2. This CME precedes and is partially overlapped by the larger CME: 2026-10-26T09:48Z, very likely from the same source. The source is newly developed AR 14561, with two distinct but close proximity eruptive signatures, likely responsible for this leading edge and CME: 2026-10-26T09:48Z. For this leading edge, the eruptive source is likely field line movement/brightening in SDO AIA 171/193, and on-disk brightening in SDO AIA 304 and STEREO A EUVI 304, starting around 2026-10-26T08:31Z and centered around S09W72. This eruption is also associated with a C1.9 flare peaking at 2026-10-26T08:38Z, observed in SDO AIA 131.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. Despite the source location around S09W72, the fit does not work unless it is around W40-W50, so we may be observing significant deflection not seen well in corresponding EUV imagery.

rows.note: CME observed to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the SE in STEREO A COR2. This CME follows the more faint CME: 2026-10-26T09:00Z, very likely from the same source. The source is newly developed AR 14561, with two distinct but close proximity eruptive signatures, likely responsible for this front and CME: 2026-10-26T09:00Z. For this CME, the eruptive source is likely an area of dimming and field line movement centered ~S05W80 in the vicinity of AR 14561, observed in SDO AIA 171/195, GOES SUVI 284, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304, starting around 2026-10-26T09:10Z. This follows separate field line movement/brightening in SDO AIA 171/193 starting around 2026-10-26T08:31Z ~S09W72, likely responsible for preceding CME: 2026-10-26T09:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. Despite the source location around S05W80, the fit does not work unless it is around W45-W50, so we may be observing significant deflection not seen well in corresponding EUV imagery.

rows.note: This CME is visible to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. This event is not visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery despite data availability, likely because it is directed towards the spacecraft and therefore occulted by the coronagraph. The source is related to an eruption and C2.8 flare from Active Region 14561 (S12W77) starting around 2026-10-26T18:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery. A subsequent opening of field lines is visible over the southwest limb as seen in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the source longitude.

rows.note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery.  This event was also seen in SOHO LASCO C3 after a downlink data gap backfilled and was seen in STEREO A COR2 after a data gap from 2026-10-26T20:38Z to 2026-10-27T02:23Z. The source is a large filament eruption visible near the eastern limb which begins to lift off around 2026-10-26T20:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 171/193/304 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284/304 imagery. The filament may extend as far as longitude E50 to beyond the east limb. A subsequent opening of field lines is visible over the northeast limb in GOES SUVI 284 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Due to a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery, a preliminary plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of -90 degrees.

Updated measurement based on available STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C3 imagery in SWPC_CAT. The measurement is based on the source location as well as the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT.

rows.note: Narrow CME visible to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and the NE in STEREO A COR2. The potential source may be a faint filament eruption best seen starting around 2026-10-27T02:16Z in GOES SUVI 304 imagery. Post-eruption dimming can also be seen in SDO AIA 193 centered around N40E20.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between GOES CCOR-1, SOHO LASCO C2/C3, and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT as well as the potential source location.

rows.note: Faint CME visible to the NE in STEREO A COR2. The CME is not clearly visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The potential source location is not found in available EUV imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane of sky measurement using STEREO A COR2 running difference imagery in SWPC_CAT.

rows.note: Faint CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source may be field line movement on/near the high latitude N limb around 2026-10-27T22:31Z in SDO AIA 171, or far-sided and unobserved.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between GOES CCOR-1, SOHO LASCO C2, and STEREO A COR2.

rows.note: Faint CME observed to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, also very faintly observed to the SW in STEREO A COR2, becoming more defined as it travels further into each coronagraph's field-of-view. The source is likely former AR 14561, located around S10W95 at this time. There is no distinct, clean eruption associated with this CME, but rather slow field line movement and brightening from this region of the disk in GOES SUVI 284 starting around 2026-10-28T09:46Z, also observed as some field line movement and brightening near AR 14561 in STEREO A EUVI 195.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2/C3 only 3D analysis using the estimated source observation ~S10W95 as a basis. As such, the parameters may vary slightly. The front is barely visible in STEREO A COR2 white light imagery but not reliably resolvable in its running difference imagery for triangulation.

rows.note: This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the east in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is a filament eruption with liftoff starting around 2026-10-29T07:36Z seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery. The footpoints extend from about S20W20 to S10W50. Post eruptive dimming is visible in SDO AIA 193 with an opening of field lines seen over the southwest limb in SDO AIA 171 and GOES SUVI 171/284 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

rows.note: Very minor and faint CME seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and in GOES CCOR-1 coronagraphs. This CME is not seen in STEREO A COR2. Its source is a very minor eruption from the former AR 14561 (S10W130) starting ~2026-10-30T11:25Z as seen in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery. AR 14561 rotated off of the Earth-facing disk on 2026-10-27.

cmeAnalyses.note: An approximate analysis based on the location of the (very minor) source and the imagery in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 coronagraphs and not confirmed by triangulation since the front is not seen in STEREO A COR2.

rows.note: CME first seen to the West by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-10-31T05:00Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME is not clearly seen in STEREO A COR2, as it may be obscured by the pylon or too faint to view clearly. The source of this event is an eruption from former AR 14561 (S11W140) beginning at approx. 2026-10-31T04:30Z as seen in STEREO A EUVI 195. Brightening near the region and dimming extending Northward can be seen in association with this eruption, possibly suggesting a Northern deflection.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1.

rows.note: Diffuse CME first seen to the SE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-11-01T00:00Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is a small filament eruption seen centered at approx. S15E65 beginning at approx. 2026-10-31T23:25Z as seen in SDO AIA 304. Post eruptive arcades and field line movement is also visible in SDO AIA 171/193. This eruption is in close proximity to a coronal hole, potentially resulting in some deflection.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

rows.note: CME first seen to the West in SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-11-01T19:00Z. The CME is also visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The CME may be faintly visible to the east in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source of this event is a filament eruption seen centered at approx. N15W15. Filament destabilization began at approx. 2026-11-01T16:43Z, with liftoff beginning at approx. 2026-11-01T17:54Z as seen in SDO AIA, STEREO A EUVI and GOES SUVI 304. Post eruptive arcades and field line movement are also visible in SDO AIA 193, GOES SUVI 284 and STEREO A EUVI 195.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2 and one frame usable frame of STEREO A COR2, noting poor quality COR2 imagery affecting front visibility beyond one frame into a real-time data gap starting 2026-11-01T19:38Z.

rows.note: Slow developing CME first seen to the NE by SOHO LASCO C2, also observed in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1, not observed in STEREO A COR due to a data gap in real-time starting at 2026-11-01T19:38Z. The source of this event is an eruption from beyond the NE limb seen in GOES SUVI 284/304 beginning at approx. 2026-11-01T18:14Z as filament ejecta and very wide, slow field line movement. An initial faint CME at 2026-11-01T18:36Z (LASCO C2) measuring plane-of-sky ~164 km/s is observed prior to this brighter emerging front.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2/C3 only plane-of-sky with no STEREO A COR2 available to triangulate the far-sided source. This front starts very slow and speeds up, altering its shape slightly with a faster nose emerging in later frames; this behavior aligns with the GOES SUVI observed erupting field line activity.
Updated measurement with later frames of STEREO A COR2 to provide a 3D longitude fit.

rows.note: Wide, slow CME observed to the E in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, not in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap beginning at 2026-11-03T18:36Z. This CME is very slow to erupt, speeding up well after its first observation in SOHO LASCO C2. The source is observed in GOES SUVI 171/195/284 starting loosely around 2026-11-03T08:00Z as wide, slow field line movement lasting several hours on/near the E limb, and source may be slightly far-sided.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C3 plane-of-sky using only later frames, as the front speeds up following most early frames.
Updated measurement using late frames of STEREO A COR2 to provide a 3D fit.

rows.note: Faint CME first seen to the NW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-11-04T02:48Z. This CME fades before exiting the field-of-view in SOHO LASCO C2, and is therefore not visible in GOES CCOR-1 or SOHO LASCO C3. This CME and source are also obscured by a data gap in STEREO A COR2 from 2026-11-03T18:23Z to 2026-11-04T04:23Z. The source of this event is field line movement seen beyond the NW limb beginning at approx. 2026-11-04T02:00Z as seen in SOD AIA 171.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky using a longitude of W90 due to source beyond the NE limb and lack of available STEREO A COR2 imagery for a 3D fit.

rows.note: CME faintly visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The potential source is unclear, but may be a small eruption seen near the northeast limb in GOES SUVI 304 as an ejecta of material starting around 2026-11-05T03:24Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1 imagery as well as the potential source location.

rows.note: CME faintly visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The CME is not clearly visible in GOES CCOR-1 or STEREO A COR2 imagery. There is no clear source for this CME seen in available EUV imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane of sky measurement using SOHO LASCO C2/C3 running difference imagery in SWPC_CAT.

rows.note: CME first seen in white light imagery to the E in GOES CCOR-1 starting at 2026-11-05T20:00Z. In real time, this CME is covered by data gaps in SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is like related to an M3.5 class flare from AR 14566 (S08E35) which peaked at 2026-11-05T18:33Z. The flare is best seen in SDO AIA 131. Some post-eruptive dimming can also be seen in SDO AIA 193. Due to the source location being in close proximity to a coronal hole, some deflection is likely.

cmeAnalyses.note: Preliminary measurement based only on running difference imagery from GOES CCOR-1. This measurement is based on the source location, but there is a high degree of uncertainty in this measurement due to the single perspective and the close proximity of the source to a coronal hole.

Updated measurement following a backfill in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 data. This measurement is based on the source location. Deflection to the East is possible for this CME due to its proximity to a coronal hole.

rows.note: CME seen to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME is also faintly visible to the east in STEREO A COR2 after a data gap from 2026-11-05T14:35Z to 2026-11-06T01:38Z. The potential source location may be a minor eruption seen near the SE limb in GOES SUVI 304 imagery starting around 2026-11-05T19:28Z located near S15E75. Moving/opening field lines are also best seen in SDO AIA 171/193 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: This measurement is based on the best fit between STEREO A COR2, SOHO LASCO C2/C3, and GOES CCOR-1 imagery in SWPC_CAT as well as the potential source location. Due to the faintness of the CME's leading edge in STEREO A COR2, there may be more uncertainty than usual in this measurement.

rows.note: Narrow CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source may possibly be a minor eruption starting around 2026-11-06T00:22Z in as best seen in SDO AIA 193, with moving field lines seen around S15E70.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT.

rows.note: Narrow CME visible to the west in STEREO A COR2. The CME is not clearly visible in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery is not available due to a downlink data gap. The potential source is an eruption seen near the west limb in STEREO A EUV 195/304 located around N20W160 starting around 2026-11-06T03:15Z. The eruption can be seen as an ejecta of material in STEREO A EUV 304. Moving field lines and post-eruption arcades are also visible in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the potential source location.

rows.note: CME visible to the NE in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME may also be faintly visible to the NNE in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The start of the CME may be faintly visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2  at the time of the analysis, but was not visible in SOHO LASCO C3 in real time due to a downlink data gap. The source is an eruption just on or beyond the NE limb as seen in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284 imagery seen as opening field lines starting at 2026-11-06T06:16Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT as well as the potential source location. Only two frames of STEREO A COR2 imagery were available for a measurement. The majority of the fit uses GOES CCOR-1 imagery.

rows.note: Wide CME visible to the NW in GOES CCOR-1 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. The CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery in real-time due to a data gap starting at 2026-11-06T13:38Z. The likely source is a filament eruption that starts to lift off in STEREO A EUV 304 imagery, around N35W140, starting at 2026-11-06T13:15Z. The filament can also be seen lifting off beyond the west limb in GOES SUVI 304 imagery.  Moving/opening field lines are also visible in SDO AIA 171 in ISWA, SDO AIA 193, and GOES SUVI 284 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location using GOES CCOR-1 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery.

Measurement of the wider, fainter, potential shock feature of the CME. This shock feature appears to move more eastward than the leading edge and bulk of the CME as seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. STEREO A COR2 imagery was not available, so this measurement is approximate.

rows.note: A very minor CME see to the NW in LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. This CME is not seen STEREO A COR2 as there is a data gap. It is possible that this CME is an outflow following the 2026-11-06T16:15Z CME. No clear source for this CME has been found.

cmeAnalyses.note: The CME imagery is only available in SOHO LASCO and GOES CCOR-1 imagery and is covered by a long data gap in STEREO A COR2. The source for this minor CME has not been found. Therefore only a plane-of-sky analysis is possible.

rows.note: Faint CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source is likely field line movement on/near the high latitude NE limb, observed starting around 2026-11-07T03:55Z in SDO AIA 171.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2, noting a deflected front making tracking with the swpc_cat tool difficult.

rows.note: First in a pair of far-sided CMEs from a filament eruption, followed by slower CME 2026-11-07T10:24Z.  This leading edge is more faint and observed to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source for both is a far-sided filament eruption, observed well in GOES SUVI 284/304 over the N limb starting around 2026-11-07T08:04Z, with the filament first lifting off as early as 2026-11-07T06:51Z. Also observed to the NW in STEREO A EUVI 195 as field line movement around 2026-11-07T08:35Z and STEREO A EUVI 304 as filament ejecta around 2026-11-07T06:15Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.
Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

rows.note: Second in a pair of far-sided CMEs from a filament eruption, following faster CME 2026-11-07T09:36Z.  This leading edge is brighter and observed to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the NW in STEREO A COR2. The source for both is a far-sided filament eruption, observed well in GOES SUVI 284/304 over the N limb starting around 2026-11-07T08:04Z, with the filament first lifting off as early as 2026-11-07T06:51Z. Also observed to the NW in STEREO A EUVI 195 as field line movement around 2026-11-07T08:35Z and STEREO A EUVI 304 as filament ejecta around 2026-11-07T06:15Z. This second CME is likely delayed filament material following the main eruption, observed deflecting eastward in GOES SUVI 304 and exiting the field-of-view by 2026-11-07T12:24Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.

rows.note: CME visible to the NW in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME may also be faintly visible in SOHO LASCO C2 imagery prior to a data gap starting at 2026-11-07T21:12Z. The CME is not clearly visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The potential source may be a filament eruption seen beyond the NW limb from the point of view of STEREO A EUV 304 imagery starting at 2026-11-07T15:45Z. The eruption can also be seen beyond the NW limb from the point of view of GOES SUVI 304 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on potential source location using GOES CCOR-1 imagery.

rows.note: Faint CME observed to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. No source is observed in EUV imagery and is likely far-sided.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

rows.note: Faint CME observed to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source may be further far-sided or observed as field line movement on the W limb in GOES SUVI 195/284 starting around 2026-11-08T05:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.
